title: Flows, limits, and cancellation
summary: Transform a cold Flow, stop after two readings, and repair a loop that ignores cancellation.

objectives.description: Transform and limit a cold Flow.
Repair a producer that ignores cancellation.
Identify the terminal operation that starts collection.

hints: Flow operators are lazy until a terminal operation collects.
take(2) completes the flow after two values.
toList collects the remaining emissions into a list.

misconceptions.description: Expecting a Flow builder to run before collection.
misconceptions.testDescription: The flow is doubled, limited, and collected with Flow operators.
misconceptions.feedback: A flow builder is cold. Nothing is emitted until collect, toList, first, or another terminal operation runs.

misconceptions.description: Collecting into a shared mutable list from several coroutines.
misconceptions.diagnostic: Collecting concurrent flows into one mutableListOf without synchronization or a Channel.
misconceptions.feedback: A plain MutableList is not thread-safe. Let each collection produce its own value, or use a Channel or StateFlow for shared state.
NonCancellable is only for cleanup that must finish. A long-running producer must observe cancellation.

misconceptions.description: Believing map or take starts a cold flow.
misconceptions.feedback: Intermediate operators return another cold flow. Only a terminal operation such as collect starts the producer.

sections.title: Flows are cold streams
sections.body: flow { emit(read()) } builds a cold stream. Each collector runs the builder again, so producers are not shared by default. Intermediate operators such as map, filter, and take return a new flow description. Terminal operations such as collect, toList, and first start the work.

sections.title: Cancellation is cooperative
sections.body: A coroutine stops only where it checks for cancellation or suspends in a cancellable call. A tight while (true) loop that never suspends keeps running after its scope is cancelled. Call currentCoroutineContext().ensureActive() inside long loops, and keep blocking work off the dispatcher. finally blocks run during cancellation, but suspending cleanup needs withContext(NonCancellable) if it must complete.

sections.title: Test flows with a controlled scope
sections.body: kotlinx-coroutines-test provides runTest, which skips delays and fails when work leaks past the test. Collect the flow with toList and compare the result. Keep take and flowOf in tests so the suite does not depend on a real sensor clock.

vocabulary.definition: A flow whose builder runs separately for each collector.
An operation such as collect or toList that starts a flow.
Cancellation that takes effect only at suspension or explicit checks.
A context used for cleanup that must finish during cancellation.

steps.prompt: Edit Main.kt. firstDoubled collects the first two readings, doubles each one, and returns them in order.

Map each reading before limiting the stream.

tests.description: The loader remains a suspend function over a Flow.
The flow is doubled, limited, and collected with Flow operators.

steps.title: The producer that never stops
steps.prompt: The rover link keeps sampling after the dashboard closes. Select the faulty instruction and the correct repair.
hints: Cancellation reaches a coroutine only at a suspension point or check.
The loop never suspends or checks the context.
steps.explanation: A tight loop with no suspension point never observes cancellation. NonCancellable explicitly hides the scope from cancellation, and swallowing CancellationException breaks structured concurrency.

steps.title: What starts the stream
steps.prompt: Which call actually starts collecting a cold Flow?
hints: Intermediate operators describe work; they do not run it.
map and take return another flow.
flowOf builds a flow rather than consuming one.
A terminal operation consumes the stream.

quiz.prompt: Which call actually starts collecting a cold Flow?
quiz.explanation: collect is a terminal operation, so it runs the builder. map and take only add intermediate stages, and flowOf creates another cold flow.
